6. In the present case, the following two questions fall for consideration before me :

(ii). Whether the noodles can be held to be misbranded because of the positive test of MSG?

sentences.text:
To answer the first question, Rule 42 (S) of the Rules is reproduced below :
"Every advertisement for and/or a package of food containing added Monosodium Glutamate, shall carry following declaration namely :
This package of .......(name of the food) contains added MONOSODIUM GULTAMATE : [NOT RECOMMENDED FOR INFANT BELOW-12 MONTHS]"
MCRC.11644/2016.
sentences._hearing_file: Hindustan Lever Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2017.json

sentences.text: As per language of the rule, in my considered view the word "added" has great significance.
sentences._hearing_file: Hindustan Lever Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2017.json

sentences.text: The aforestated declaration is required only when MSG is added from outside source in a particular food product and such declaration is not required when MSG is present in the food product in natural form.
sentences._hearing_file: Hindustan Lever Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2017.json

sentences.text: A Public Analyst can describe a food product misbranded in terms of Rule 42 (S) of the Rules only when he gives a definite finding based on test-results that MSG is added in the food product from outside source.
sentences._hearing_file: Hindustan Lever Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 23 November, 2017.json

sentences.text:
My aforesaid interpretation of Rule 42 (S) of the Rules is fortified by the decisions rendered in C.L. Yadav and another (Supra) and Vinay Hegde and Another (Supra).

opennyai_summary.19_April_2017__facts:
The present petition u/S 482 Cr.P.C. assails the prosecution lodged by the respondent/State against the petitioner for having violated Rule 42(S) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, inter-alia on the ground that petitioner is the Manager of Hindustan Lever Ltd. which took over the erstwhile Brookbond Company on 21.03.1997 by way of amalgamation, whereas the offence in question was committed on 21.12.1996 and therefore by relying upon the decision of Single Bench of Bombay High Court in the case of Hindustan Lever Ltd.
Vs. State of Maharashtra
reported in 2009(2)FAC 4, it is submitted that the proceedings of amalgamation do not lead to transferring of criminal liability.
opennyai_summary.19_April_2017__decision:
In view of the above, as an interim measure, it is directed that the proceedings in Criminal Case No.
2473/2007 pending before the JMFC Gwalior shall remain stayed until further orders.

Presently, there is no analytical method to determine whether MSG was added to the product during its manufacture or was naturally present in the product.

, the Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd is merged with Hindustan Lever Ltd, the petitioner herein with effect from 20.3.1997.
It is settled law that a criminal liability of transferor company into the tranferee company cannot be transferred or fastened on transferee company upon its amalgamation, because with the amalgamation, the transferor company suffers a civil death and it is ceased to exist.
In the present case, the offence is occurred on 21.12.1996 and the Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd merged with the Hindustan Lever Ltd on 20.3.1997.
Thus, the Brooke Bond Lipton India Co. Ltd. committed the alleged offence before its merger with the petitioner Hindustan Lever India Co. Ltd.
